Paper walk-through · multi-drone cable transport

DiffCoord

Differentiable Coordination for Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization

DiffCoord learns a multi-drone planner's settings by computing exact gradients through the planner. The gradient math has the same three-step shape as the planner, so it reuses the planner's work.

ProblemPlannerLearningMirrorLQRDronesResultsCaveats
ADMM
Split one big problem into small ones. Charge a price when their answers disagree.
DDP
Differential dynamic programming. Fit a quadratic around a path, solve it backward in time, repeat.
LQR
Linear quadratic regulator. Linear dynamics, quadratic cost, exact backward solution.
Meta-learning
Train across many tasks so the settings also work on new ones.

Symbols: \(\vx\) state, \(\vu\) control, \(i\) agent, \(k\) time step, \(a\) ADMM round, \(\vth\) settings, \(\tilde{\ }\) safe copy, \(\vtau=\{\vx,\vu\}\) a full path. Indices are dropped where they add nothing. Numbers at the right edge are the paper's equation numbers.

§II-A · The problem

Many drones, one payload

Cables tie every drone to the same load, so no drone can plan alone. Solving for all of them at once scales poorly as the team grows.

\[\begin{aligned} \min_{\{\vx_i,\vu_i\}}\ & \sum_{i=1}^{n} J_i(\vx_i,\vu_i) \\ \text{s.t.}\ & \vx_{i,k+1}=\vf_i(\vx_{i,k},\vu_{i,k}) && \text{own dynamics} \\ & \vg_{i,k}(\vx_{i,k},\vu_{i,k})\le 0 && \text{own limits} \\ & \hd{\vh_{ij,k}(\dots)=0} && \hd{\text{shared}} \\ & \hd{\vg_{ij,k}(\dots)\le 0} && \hd{\text{shared}} \end{aligned}\]
eq 1

The red lines link agents, for example fixed cable length and minimum drone spacing. They are why this cannot be split trivially.

§II-B · Algorithm 1

The planner splits the work three ways

Each agent keeps a plan and a safe copy of that plan. The plan obeys dynamics. The copy obeys constraints. ADMM pushes the two to match.

\[\vx_{i,k}=\tx_{i,k},\qquad \vu_{i,k}=\tu_{i,k},\qquad \forall i\]
eq 3

1. DDP per agent

\[\{\vx_i,\vu_i\}^a=\arg\min\sum_k\hat\ell_{i,k}^{\,a}\]
eq 5
\[\begin{aligned}\hat\ell={}&\ell+\tfrac{\rho}{2}\big\|\vx-\tx^{a-1}+\tfrac{\vnu^{a-1}}{\rho}\big\|^2\\&+\tfrac{\sigma}{2}\big\|\vu-\tu^{a-1}+\tfrac{\vxi^{a-1}}{\sigma}\big\|^2\end{aligned}\]
eq 6

2. Nonlinear solve per time step

\[\begin{aligned}\{\tx_k,\tu_k\}^a=\arg\min&\sum_i\big(e_{x_i}^2+e_{u_i}^2\big)\\\text{s.t.}\quad&\vg\le 0,\ \ \vh=0\end{aligned}\]
eq 7

\(e^2\) terms are the same two penalties as in (6), now on the copies. Dynamics are absent, so each step is a small static problem.

3. Price update

\[\vnu^a=\vnu^{a-1}+\rho(\vx-\tx)\]
eq 9a
\[\vxi^a=\vxi^{a-1}+\sigma(\vu-\tu)\]
eq 9b

Example \(\rho=2,\ x=1.0,\ \tilde x=0.7\). The gap is 0.3, so \(\nu\) goes from 0 to 0.6. Next round, (6) pulls \(x\) toward \(\tilde x-\nu/\rho=0.4\), so \(x\) drops toward its copy.

§III · What gets learned

A small network picks the settings

Settings \(\vth\) are cost weights (what the plan cares about) and ADMM penalties \(\rho,\sigma\) (how hard agents must agree). Hand tuning is slow, and with few ADMM rounds the two kinds interact.

\[\vth_i=\pi_i(\chi_i;\varpi_i)\]
eq 18
\[\min_{\{\varpi_i\}}\ L_{\rm m}=\frac1M\sum_{t=1}^{M}L_t\big(\{\vtau_{i,t}^{a_{\rm f}},\ttau_{i,t}^{a_{\rm f}}\}\big)\]
eq 19

Outer level: tune network weights \(\varpi\) over \(M\) tasks. Inner level: run the planner for \(a_{\rm f}\) rounds. No expert trajectories are needed: \(L_t\) scores task error plus the gap \(\|\vtau-\ttau\|^2\).

\[\frac{\dd L_{\rm m}}{\dd\varpi}= \underbrace{\frac{\partial L}{\partial\vtau}}_{\text{a formula}}\ \underbrace{\hd{\frac{\dd\vtau}{\dd\vth}}}_{\hd{\text{out of a solver}}}\ \underbrace{\frac{\partial\vth}{\partial\varpi}}_{\text{backprop}}\]
eq 20, short

Two of the three factors are easy. The red one is the hard part, and the rest of the paper is about it.

§IV · The key idea

The gradient solver mirrors the planner

Differentiate each planner step and you get a matching gradient step. Top half of the paper's figure: planner. Bottom half: its twin.

Here \(\mX=\dd\vx/\dd\vth\) and \(\mU=\dd\vu/\dd\vth\). They are matrices: one column per setting.

For one agent, \(\mX\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times p}\), where \(p\) is the total number of settings.

Same ADMM penalties, same round budget, same parallel split. There is no second solver to tune.

Planner: finds the path
Reused
Gradient solver: finds how the path moves

Step 1: DDP becomes LQR

\[\delta\vu=\re{\vK}\,\delta\vx+\hat{\boldsymbol{k}}\]
eq 13
\[\hat V^{xx}=\hat Q^{xx}-\re{\hat Q^{xu}(\hat Q^{uu})^{-1}}\hat Q^{ux}\]
eq 14b
Feedback gain \(\vK\), \((\hat Q^{uu})^{-1}\), \(\hat V^{xx}\), Jacobians
\[\mU=\re{\vK}\,\mX+\bw{\boldsymbol{K}^{\rm ff}}\]
eq 31a
\[\bw{\hat V^{x\theta}}=\hat Q^{x\theta}-\re{\hat Q^{xu}(\hat Q^{uu})^{-1}}\hat Q^{u\theta}\]
eq 29

Step 2: nonlinear solve becomes a quadratic program

\[\min\ \sum_i(e_{x_i}^2+e_{u_i}^2)\quad\text{s.t. }\vg\le0,\ \vh=0\]
eq 7
Hard constraints, solved with ipopt.
Split by time step, \(\rho\), \(\sigma\)
\[\min_{\boldsymbol{Z}}\ \operatorname{tr}\!\big(\tfrac12\boldsymbol{Z}^\top\hat L^{\tilde\tau\tilde\tau}\boldsymbol{Z}+(\hat L^{\tilde\tau\theta})^\top\boldsymbol{Z}\big)\]
eq 34
\(\boldsymbol{Z}=[\tX;\tU]\). Constraints are softened first, see below.

Step 3: price update becomes its derivative

\[\vnu^a=\vnu^{a-1}+\re{\rho}(\vx-\tx)\]
eq 9a
\(\rho\), \(\sigma\)
\[\frac{\dd\vnu^a}{\dd\vth}=\frac{\dd\vnu^{a-1}}{\dd\vth}+\re{\rho}(\mX-\tX)+\nabla_{\vth}\vnu^a\]
eq 38a
\[\hat H^{x\theta}=\nabla_{\vth}\hat H^{x}-\rho\,\hd{\frac{\dd\tx^{a-1}}{\dd\vth}}+\hd{\frac{\dd\vnu^{a-1}}{\dd\vth}}\]
eq 27a

The dashed links in math form. Last round's gradients (red) enter this round's LQR as a linear cost. This coupling is what a single-agent method never has to handle.

\[\begin{aligned}\hat{\mathcal{L}}_k={}&\sum_i\big(e_{x_i}^2+e_{u_i}^2\big)+\frac{1}{2\mu}\sum_{i}\sum_{j\ne i}h_{ij}^2\\&-\mu\sum_i\Big[\ln(-g_i)+\sum_{j\ne i}\ln(-g_{ij})\Big]\end{aligned}\]
eq 33

Constraints that switch on and off break gradients. So, for the gradient step only, they become smooth barrier terms with \(\mu=10^{-6}\). The plan itself still uses hard constraints.

§IV-A · Lemmas 1 and 2

Why the trajectory gradient is an LQR

Differentiating DDP's optimality conditions gives equations that are themselves the solution of an LQR. That LQR costs \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) in the horizon length \(N\).

  1. At the optimum

    The slope with respect to \(\vu\) is zero, and the path obeys dynamics.

    \[\boldsymbol{0}=\hat Q^{u}(\vx,\vu,\tu^{a-1},\vxi^{a-1},\vth)\]
    eq 21
    \[\hat V^{x}=\hat Q^{x}(\vx,\vu,\tx^{a-1},\vnu^{a-1},\vth)\]
    eq 22

  2. Differentiate by \(\vth\)

    This is the implicit function theorem: get the slope of a solution without unrolling the solver.

    \[\boldsymbol{0}=\hat Q^{ux}\frac{\dd\vx}{\dd\vth}+\hat Q^{uu}\frac{\dd\vu}{\dd\vth}+\hat Q^{u\theta}\]
    eq 24b
    \[\frac{\dd\vx_{k+1}}{\dd\vth}=f^{x}\frac{\dd\vx}{\dd\vth}+f^{u}\frac{\dd\vu}{\dd\vth}+f^{\theta}\]
    eq 24c

  3. Spot an LQR

    Those equations are the optimality conditions of this problem, so its answer is the gradient.

    \[\min_{\mX,\mU}\sum_{k}\operatorname{tr}\!\Big(\tfrac12\begin{bmatrix}\mX\\\mU\end{bmatrix}^{\!\top}\!\hat H^{\tau\tau}\begin{bmatrix}\mX\\\mU\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}\hat H^{x\theta}\\\hat H^{u\theta}\end{bmatrix}^{\!\top}\!\begin{bmatrix}\mX\\\mU\end{bmatrix}\Big)\]
    eq 26
    \[\text{s.t. }\ \mX_{k+1}=f^{x}\mX+f^{u}\mU+f^{\theta},\quad\mX_0=\boldsymbol{0}\]
    eq 26

  4. Solve it fast

    One backward sweep, one forward sweep. Almost everything is already stored from DDP.

    \[\bw{\boldsymbol{K}^{\rm ff}}=-\re{(\hat Q^{uu})^{-1}}\hat Q^{u\theta}\]
    eq 30
    \[\mU=\re{\vK}\mX+\bw{\boldsymbol{K}^{\rm ff}},\quad\mX_{k+1}=f^{x}\mX+f^{u}\mU+f^{\theta}\]
    eq 31

Tiny example, one control and no dynamics

Problem, with \(q=3,\ r=1\):

\[\min_u\ \tfrac12q(u-1)^2+\tfrac12ru^2\]

Slope zero gives the plan:

\[u^*=\frac{q}{q+r}=0.75\]

Equation (30) gives the gradient:

\[\frac{\dd u^*}{\dd q}=-\frac{1}{\re{4}}(-0.25)=0.0625\]

Here \(\hat Q^{uq}=u^*-1=-0.25\). The green 4 is \(\hat Q^{uu}=q+r\), which the planner already computed. Check: \(q=3.01\) gives \(u^*=0.75062\), a slope of about 0.062.

§V · Multilift

On drones, the agents are the payload and the cables

The paper plans with cable dynamics instead of drone dynamics, which is cheaper. Each drone's position then follows directly from its cable.

\[\vp_i=\vp_l+\vR_l\vr_i+l_i\vd_i\]
eq 42

Drone position = payload position + attachment point + cable vector.

\[\vt_k=\vP^{\dagger}\begin{bmatrix}\vR_l^\top\vF_l\\\vM_l\end{bmatrix}+\vN\boldsymbol{\Pi}_k\]
eq 48c

The force and torque needed on the payload do not fix the tensions. With 4 cables there are 12 tension numbers and 6 equations, so 6 are free. \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_k\) picks them.

\[\rho^a=\mathrm{Sig}^a(\alpha_\rho)\,\rho,\qquad\mathrm{Sig}^a(\alpha)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-\alpha(a-a_{\rm offset})}}\]
eq 49

Penalties change by round. The net learns base \(\rho\) and shape \(\alpha\). The paper sets \(a_{\rm offset}\) to the middle round. With \(\alpha=2\) and rounds 1, 2, 3 the multipliers are 0.12, 0.50, 0.88, so the push to agree gets stronger.

\[L_t=w_p\ell_{l,p}^t+w_r\ell_{l,r}^t+\sum_{i=1}^n\big(w_p\ell_{i,p}^t+w_r\ell_{i,r}^t\big)\]
eq 50

\(\ell_p\): tracking error. \(\ell_r\): plan vs copy gap. Subscript \(l\): payload. Subscript \(i\): cable.

§VI · Results

Fast to train, and it flies on teams it never saw

Training used 10 tasks on a 4-drone team. Each task moves the payload's balance point.

Three rounds are enough

Final loss drops sharply from 2 to 3 rounds, then mostly levels off. Paper Fig. 4a.

Gradients take about a third of the time

1.94 ms against 5.67 and 7.09 ms, at \(N=100\). All three agree to within \(10^{-8}\) relative error. ADDP's dark band is an extra matrix, \(V^{\theta\theta}\), that never reaches the answer. Paper Fig. 6a.

Step 2 is the one that grows with team size

4 to 12 drones: 9.05 to 79.30 ms, because tension links every drone. Steps 1 and 3 barely move. Paper Fig. 5.

4 drones. Doubling \(N\) from 100 to 200 roughly doubles step 1, matching \(\mathcal{O}(N)\). Paper Table I.

The plan changes with the task

Left, Task 5, most off-center: tensions are uneven and cables tilt more. Right, Task 8, least off-center: tensions stay close together. Paper Fig. 11.

3 drones through a window at 2.5 m/s

The team folds into a line to fit. Real flight roughly matches the planned formation. Paper Fig. 13.

6 drones through a horizontal gap, over 2.5 m/s

The team spreads apart, then regroups. The paper reports no earlier real flight of this kind. Paper Fig. 16.

Payload feedback uses the gain DDP already computed

Each flight carried a 200 g water bottle 5 cm off-center on a tray. Each drone ran its own stock PX4 controller, with no drone-to-drone communication. Sloshing was not in the plan, so the payload gain \(\vK\) corrects for it in flight.

\[\Delta\vt_k=\vP^{\dagger}\begin{bmatrix}\vR_l^{\top}&\boldsymbol{0}\\\boldsymbol{0}&\boldsymbol{I}\end{bmatrix}\re{\vK_{l,k}^{a_{\rm f}}}\big(\vx_{l,k}^{\rm fb}-\vx_{l,k}^{a_{\rm f}}\big)\]
eq 52

Payload error → tension fix → position fix for each drone.

Feedback cuts tracking error by up to 41.2%. It cuts tilt in the gap by up to 60.9% with 3 drones and 83.7% with 6. Without it, one 3-drone run hit the obstacle (paper Fig. 15e).

Caveats

What to keep in mind

  • Step 2 is the bottleneck. Its gradient time grows about 9-fold from 4 to 12 drones. The paper says fixing each agent's neighbor set removes this growth for swarms without dense coupling.
  • Small training set. 10 tasks, and the task input is only the payload offset. This is my reading, not a claim in the paper.
  • The budget is fixed. Training assumes 3 rounds and a fixed penalty schedule per task. Adaptive budgets and feedback-based penalties are the paper's future work, along with changing environments.
  • Planning takes about a second. Stage 2 alone took 0.93 s (3 drones, 6 s plan) and 1.2 s (6 drones, 5 s plan) on a CPU.

Figures, tables, equations and results come from the DiffCoord paper in papers/diffcoord. The PDF shows no author names. Equation (20) is shortened and indices are dropped throughout. The drawn diagrams, the small worked examples and the caveats section were written for this page.
